extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural, grade-school science multiple-choice questions partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, accompanied by the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences, created to encourage AI research in advanced question answering requiring reasoning and commonsense knowledge.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were gathered through several months of extensive search and investigation from standardized test practice and released exams across various state and national educational assessment programs, as well as an anonymous partner. The supporting ARC Corpus was collected by querying a major search engine using automatically generated queries based on 100 hand-written templates across 80 science topics, collecting top documents, de-duplicating them, extracting text, chunking into sentences, and augmenting with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Standardized science tests from US state assessment programs (including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, CA Stnds Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assm. Prog, MD School Assm., MCAS, MEA, MEAP, MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achieve. Tests, TAKS, VA Stds of Learning, WASL), TIMSS assessments, questions from an anonymous content partner ('Mercury'), and publically releasable questions from the Kaggle 2016 Allen AI Science Challenge. For the ARC Corpus: Web documents retrieved via search engine queries, Simple Wikipedia articles tagged as science, and Wiktionary dictionary definitions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to include non-diagram, multiple-choice questions (typically 4-way) spanning 3rd to 9th grade levels. They were partitioned into a Challenge Set (questions answered incorrectly by both an Information Retrieval solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information solver) and an Easy Set (the remainder). For the ARC Corpus, top retrieved documents were de-duplicated, content was stripped down to text, and text was chunked into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note a retrieval bias in underlying IR methods toward sentences that are highly similar to the entire question, biasing away from sentences that individually only partially match the question but together fully explain the answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to non-diagram multiple-choice questions. In entailment baseline adaptations, naive conversion of questions to assertions can result in non-grammatical sentences. The operational definition of the Challenge Set is an approximation of difficulty based on two specific baseline solvers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, testing, and validation of advanced question-answering, machine reading comprehension, and natural language reasoning models.
